rules.rule_name: Program Initialization
rules.rule_description: At the start of each program execution, all error indicators, user-modification flags, and message fields are reset to ensure a clean processing state.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
1: Program Initialization
Initialize error flags, user-modified flags,
clear message fields

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Add Transaction program is invoked
acceptance_criteria.When: The program begins execution
acceptance_criteria.Then: The error flag is set to OFF, the user-modified flag is set to NO, the screen message field (WS-MESSAGE) is cleared to spaces, and the error message output field (ERRMSGO) on the Add Transaction screen is cleared to spaces

rules.rule_name: Session Validation and Redirect to Sign-On
rules.rule_description: If no active session context exists when the program is invoked, the user must be redirected to the Sign-On screen to establish a valid session before proceeding.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
2: Session Validation
Redirect to Sign-On Screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Add Transaction program is invoked
acceptance_criteria.When: No communication area exists (session length equals zero, indicating no active session)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The target program is set to 'COSGN00C' (Sign-On screen) and control is transferred to that program, preventing access to the Add Transaction function without a valid session

rules.rule_name: First-Time Screen Display and Pre-Population
rules.rule_description: On the first entry to the Add Transaction screen, the screen is initialized and, if a transaction was pre-selected from a prior screen, the Card Number field is pre-populated and processing begins automatically.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
3: First-Time Screen Display
Initialize Add Transaction Screen
Pre-populate Card Number if selected

acceptance_criteria.Given: A valid session exists and the user is entering the Add Transaction screen for the first time (program re-entry flag is not set)
acceptance_criteria.When: The program detects it is the initial entry
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program marks itself as re-enterable, clears the screen output area to LOW-VALUES, positions the cursor on the Account ID field, and if a pre-selected transaction value (CDEMO-CT02-TRN-SELECTED) is present (not spaces and not LOW-VALUES), it is moved into the Card Number input field and the Enter Key processing logic is immediately invoked; the Add Transaction screen is then displayed to the user

rules.rule_name: Screen Input Reception
rules.rule_description: When a returning user interacts with the Add Transaction screen, the system receives and captures all input data entered by the user for subsequent processing.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
4: Screen Input Reception
Receive user input from
Add Transaction Screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: A valid session exists and the user has previously been presented with the Add Transaction screen (program re-entry flag is set)
acceptance_criteria.When: The user submits input from the Add Transaction screen (map COTRN2A, mapset COTRN02)
acceptance_criteria.Then: All user-entered data is received into the input map area (COTRN2AI) and made available for key-press evaluation and business logic processing

rules.rule_name: Enter Key Processing Routing
rules.rule_description: When the user presses the Enter key, the system routes processing to the full validation and transaction addition workflow.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
5: Enter Key Processing
Route to validation and
transaction add logic

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has submitted input from the Add Transaction screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The key pressed is the Enter key (DFHENTER)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system invokes the input key field validation, input data field validation, and confirmation check sequence to process the transaction addition request

rules.rule_name: Navigate Back to Previous Screen
rules.rule_description: When the user presses PF3, the system navigates back to the program that invoked the Add Transaction screen, or defaults to the main menu if no calling program is recorded.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
6: Navigate Back
Return to calling program
or default menu

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has submitted input from the Add Transaction screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses PF3
acceptance_criteria.Then: If a calling program is recorded in CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM (not spaces and not LOW-VALUES), control is transferred to that program; otherwise, control is transferred to the default menu program 'COMEN01C'; in both cases, the current transaction ID and program name are recorded as the originating context, and the program context counter is reset to zero

rules.rule_name: Clear Screen on PF4
rules.rule_description: When the user presses PF4, all input fields on the Add Transaction screen are cleared, presenting a blank form for new data entry.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
7: Clear Screen
Clear all input fields
Redisplay blank form

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has submitted input from the Add Transaction screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses PF4
acceptance_criteria.Then: All input fields are cleared to spaces (Account ID, Card Number, Type Code, Category Code, Source, Amount, Description, Original Date, Processing Date, Merchant ID, Merchant Name, Merchant City, Merchant Zip, Confirm), the cursor is positioned on the Account ID field, the message field is cleared, and the blank Add Transaction screen is redisplayed

rules.rule_name: Copy Last Transaction Data on PF5
rules.rule_description: When the user presses PF5, the system retrieves the most recently added transaction from the transaction file and pre-populates the transaction detail fields on the screen, allowing the user to reuse prior transaction details.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
8: Copy Last Transaction Data
Retrieve most recent transaction
Pre-populate all detail fields

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has submitted input from the Add Transaction screen with a valid Account ID or Card Number entered
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses PF5
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system first validates the Account ID or Card Number; if valid, it browses the transaction file from the highest key backwards to retrieve the last transaction record, and if no error exists, it copies the following fields from the last transaction to the screen: Type Code, Category Code, Source, Amount (formatted), Description, Original Date, Processing Date, Merchant ID, Merchant Name, Merchant City, and Merchant Zip; the Enter Key processing logic is then invoked to validate and prompt for confirmation

rules.rule_name: Invalid Key Handling
rules.rule_description: When the user presses any key other than Enter, PF3, PF4, or PF5, the system displays an invalid key error message.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
9: Invalid Key Handling
Display invalid key message

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has submitted input from the Add Transaction screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses any key other than Enter, PF3, PF4, or PF5
acceptance_criteria.Then: The error flag is set to 'Y', the standard invalid key message (CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY) is placed in the message field, and the Add Transaction screen is redisplayed with the error message

rules.rule_name: Account ID Numeric Validation
rules.rule_description: When an Account ID is provided, it must contain only numeric characters before a cross-reference lookup can be performed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
10: Account ID Validation
Verify Account ID is numeric

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has entered a value in the Account ID field (not spaces and not LOW-VALUES) on the Add Transaction screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The Account ID field is evaluated during key field validation
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the Account ID value is not numeric, the error flag is set to 'Y', the message 'Account ID must be Numeric...' is displayed, the cursor is positioned on the Account ID field, and the screen is redisplayed; if the Account ID is numeric, it is converted to a numeric value and processing continues to the Account ID cross-reference lookup

rules.rule_name: Account ID Cross-Reference Lookup
rules.rule_description: A valid numeric Account ID is looked up in the Account Cross-Reference file (CXACAIX) to retrieve the associated Card Number, which is then auto-populated on the screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
11: Account ID Lookup
Look up Account ID to
retrieve Card Number

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account ID has been validated as numeric and converted to its numeric form
acceptance_criteria.When: The system performs a lookup of the Account ID in the Account Cross-Reference Alternate Index file (CXACAIX)
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the Account ID is found, the corresponding Card Number from the cross-reference record is moved into the Card Number input field (CARDNINI) on the screen and processing continues to data field validation; if the Account ID is not found, the error flag is set to 'Y', the message 'Account ID NOT found...' is displayed, the cursor is positioned on the Account ID field, and the screen is redisplayed

rules.rule_name: Card Number Numeric Validation
rules.rule_description: When a Card Number is provided (and no Account ID is entered), it must contain only numeric characters before a cross-reference lookup can be performed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
12: Card Number Validation
Verify Card Number is numeric

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account ID field is empty and the user has entered a value in the Card Number field (not spaces and not LOW-VALUES) on the Add Transaction screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The Card Number field is evaluated during key field validation
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the Card Number value is not numeric, the error flag is set to 'Y', the message 'Card Number must be Numeric...' is displayed, the cursor is positioned on the Card Number field, and the screen is redisplayed; if the Card Number is numeric, it is converted to a numeric value and processing continues to the Card Number cross-reference lookup

rules.rule_name: Card Number Cross-Reference Lookup
rules.rule_description: A valid numeric Card Number is looked up in the Card Cross-Reference file (CCXREF) to retrieve the associated Account ID, which is then auto-populated on the screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
13: Card Number Lookup
Look up Card Number to
retrieve Account ID

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Card Number has been validated as numeric and converted to its numeric form
acceptance_criteria.When: The system performs a lookup of the Card Number in the Card Cross-Reference file (CCXREF)
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the Card Number is found, the corresponding Account ID from the cross-reference record is moved into the Account ID input field (ACTIDINI) on the screen and processing continues to data field validation; if the Card Number is not found, the error flag is set to 'Y', the message 'Card Number NOT found...' is displayed, the cursor is positioned on the Card Number field, and the screen is redisplayed

rules.rule_name: Account or Card Number Presence Check
rules.rule_description: At least one of Account ID or Card Number must be provided by the user to identify the account for the transaction being added.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
14: Account or Card Number
Presence Check
Ensure at least one is provided

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has submitted the Add Transaction screen
acceptance_criteria.When: Both the Account ID field and the Card Number field are empty (spaces or LOW-VALUES)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The error flag is set to 'Y', the message 'Account or Card Number must be entered...' is displayed, the cursor is positioned on the Account ID field, and the screen is redisplayed; transaction processing cannot proceed without at least one identifier

rules.rule_name: Transaction Type Code Validation
rules.rule_description: The Transaction Type Code is a mandatory numeric field that must be provided and must contain only numeric characters.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
15: Transaction Type Code Validation
Verify not empty and numeric

acceptance_criteria.Given: Account ID or Card Number has been successfully validated and cross-referenced
acceptance_criteria.When: The Transaction Type Code field (TTYPCDI) is evaluated during data field validation
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the Type Code is empty (spaces or LOW-VALUES), the error flag is set to 'Y', the message 'Type CD can NOT be empty...' is displayed, the cursor is positioned on the Type Code field, and the screen is redisplayed; if the Type Code is present but not numeric, the error flag is set to 'Y', the message 'Type CD must be Numeric...' is displayed, the cursor is positioned on the Type Code field, and the screen is redisplayed; if the Type Code is present and numeric, processing continues

rules.rule_name: Transaction Category Code Validation
rules.rule_description: The Transaction Category Code is a mandatory numeric field that must be provided and must contain only numeric characters.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
16: Transaction Category Code Validation
Verify not empty and numeric

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Code has been successfully validated
acceptance_criteria.When: The Transaction Category Code field (TCATCDI) is evaluated during data field validation
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the Category Code is empty (spaces or LOW-VALUES), the error flag is set to 'Y', the message 'Category CD can NOT be empty...' is displayed, the cursor is positioned on the Category Code field, and the screen is redisplayed; if the Category Code is present but not numeric, the error flag is set to 'Y', the message 'Category CD must be Numeric...' is displayed, the cursor is positioned on the Category Code field, and the screen is redisplayed; if the Category Code is present and numeric, processing continues

rules.rule_name: Transaction Source Validation
rules.rule_description: The Transaction Source is a mandatory field that must be provided before the transaction can be added.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
17: Transaction Source Validation
Verify not empty

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Category Code has been successfully validated
acceptance_criteria.When: The Transaction Source field (TRNSRCI) is evaluated during data field validation
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the Source field is empty (spaces or LOW-VALUES), the error flag is set to 'Y', the message 'Source can NOT be empty...' is displayed, the cursor is positioned on the Source field, and the screen is redisplayed; if the Source field contains a value, processing continues

rules.rule_name: Transaction Description Validation
rules.rule_description: The Transaction Description is a mandatory field that must be provided before the transaction can be added.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
18: Transaction Description Validation
Verify not empty

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Source has been successfully validated
acceptance_criteria.When: The Transaction Description field (TDESCI) is evaluated during data field validation
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the Description field is empty (spaces or LOW-VALUES), the error flag is set to 'Y', the message 'Description can NOT be empty...' is displayed, the cursor is positioned on the Description field, and the screen is redisplayed; if the Description field contains a value, processing continues

rules.rule_name: Transaction Amount Format Validation
rules.rule_description: The Transaction Amount is mandatory and must follow a strict format: a sign character followed by 8 numeric digits, a decimal point, and 2 numeric decimal digits.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
19: Transaction Amount Validation
Verify format: sign+8digits.2digits

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Description has been successfully validated
acceptance_criteria.When: The Transaction Amount field (TRNAMTI) is evaluated during data field validation
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the Amount field is empty (spaces or LOW-VALUES), the error flag is set to 'Y', the message 'Amount can NOT be empty...' is displayed, the cursor is positioned on the Amount field, and the screen is redisplayed; if the Amount is present but does not conform to the format where position 1 is '+' or '-', positions 2 through 9 (8 characters) are numeric, position 10 is '.', and positions 11 through 12 (2 characters) are numeric, then the error flag is set to 'Y', the message 'Amount should be in format -99999999.99' is displayed, the cursor is positioned on the Amount field, and the screen is redisplayed; if the Amount is valid, it is converted to a numeric value and reformatted to the standard display format before processing continues

rules.rule_name: Origination Date Format Validation
rules.rule_description: The Transaction Origination Date is mandatory and must conform to the YYYY-MM-DD format with correct positional separators.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
20: Origination Date Format Validation
Verify YYYY-MM-DD format

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Amount has been successfully validated
acceptance_criteria.When: The Origination Date field (TORIGDTI) is evaluated during data field validation
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the Origination Date is empty (spaces or LOW-VALUES), the error flag is set to 'Y', the message 'Orig Date can NOT be empty...' is displayed, the cursor is positioned on the Origination Date field, and the screen is redisplayed; if the Origination Date is present but does not conform to the format where positions 1-4 are numeric (year), position 5 is '-', positions 6-7 are numeric (month), position 8 is '-', and positions 9-10 are numeric (day), then the error flag is set to 'Y', the message 'Orig Date should be in format YYYY-MM-DD' is displayed, the cursor is positioned on the Origination Date field, and the screen is redisplayed; if the format is valid, processing continues

rules.rule_name: Processing Date Format Validation
rules.rule_description: The Transaction Processing Date is mandatory and must conform to the YYYY-MM-DD format with correct positional separators.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
21: Processing Date Format Validation
Verify YYYY-MM-DD format

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Origination Date format has been successfully validated
acceptance_criteria.When: The Processing Date field (TPROCDTI) is evaluated during data field validation
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the Processing Date is empty (spaces or LOW-VALUES), the error flag is set to 'Y', the message 'Proc Date can NOT be empty...' is displayed, the cursor is positioned on the Processing Date field, and the screen is redisplayed; if the Processing Date is present but does not conform to the format where positions 1-4 are numeric (year), position 5 is '-', positions 6-7 are numeric (month), position 8 is '-', and positions 9-10 are numeric (day), then the error flag is set to 'Y', the message 'Proc Date should be in format YYYY-MM-DD' is displayed, the cursor is positioned on the Processing Date field, and the screen is redisplayed; if the format is valid, processing continues

rules.rule_name: Origination Date Calendar Validation
rules.rule_description: After format validation, the Origination Date must be verified as a real calendar date by invoking the date validation utility CSUTLDTC.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
22: Origination Date Calendar Validation
Call CSUTLDTC to confirm valid date

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Origination Date has passed format validation
acceptance_criteria.When: The date validation utility CSUTLDTC is called with the Origination Date value and the expected date format
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the utility returns a severity code of '0000' (success), the date is accepted as valid and processing continues; if the utility returns any other severity code and the message number is not '2513', the error flag is set to 'Y', the message 'Orig Date - Not a valid date...' is displayed, the cursor is positioned on the Origination Date field, and the screen is redisplayed

rules.rule_name: Processing Date Calendar Validation
rules.rule_description: After format validation, the Processing Date must be verified as a real calendar date by invoking the date validation utility CSUTLDTC.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
23: Processing Date Calendar Validation
Call CSUTLDTC to confirm valid date

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Processing Date has passed format validation
acceptance_criteria.When: The date validation utility CSUTLDTC is called with the Processing Date value and the expected date format
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the utility returns a severity code of '0000' (success), the date is accepted as valid and processing continues; if the utility returns any other severity code and the message number is not '2513', the error flag is set to 'Y', the message 'Proc Date - Not a valid date...' is displayed, the cursor is positioned on the Processing Date field, and the screen is redisplayed

rules.rule_name: Merchant ID Validation
rules.rule_description: The Merchant ID is a mandatory numeric field that must be provided and must contain only numeric characters.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
24: Merchant ID Validation
Verify not empty and numeric

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Processing Date has been successfully validated
acceptance_criteria.When: The Merchant ID field (MIDI) is evaluated during data field validation
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the Merchant ID is empty (spaces or LOW-VALUES), the error flag is set to 'Y', the message 'Merchant ID can NOT be empty...' is displayed, the cursor is positioned on the Merchant ID field, and the screen is redisplayed; if the Merchant ID is present but not numeric, the error flag is set to 'Y', the message 'Merchant ID must be Numeric...' is displayed, the cursor is positioned on the Merchant ID field, and the screen is redisplayed; if the Merchant ID is present and numeric, processing continues

rules.rule_name: Merchant Name Validation
rules.rule_description: The Merchant Name is a mandatory field that must be provided before the transaction can be added.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
25: Merchant Name Validation
Verify not empty

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Merchant ID has been successfully validated
acceptance_criteria.When: The Merchant Name field (MNAMEI) is evaluated during data field validation
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the Merchant Name field is empty (spaces or LOW-VALUES), the error flag is set to 'Y', the message 'Merchant Name can NOT be empty...' is displayed, the cursor is positioned on the Merchant Name field, and the screen is redisplayed; if the Merchant Name field contains a value, processing continues

rules.rule_name: Merchant City Validation
rules.rule_description: The Merchant City is a mandatory field that must be provided before the transaction can be added.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
26: Merchant City Validation
Verify not empty

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Merchant Name has been successfully validated
acceptance_criteria.When: The Merchant City field (MCITYI) is evaluated during data field validation
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the Merchant City field is empty (spaces or LOW-VALUES), the error flag is set to 'Y', the message 'Merchant City can NOT be empty...' is displayed, the cursor is positioned on the Merchant City field, and the screen is redisplayed; if the Merchant City field contains a value, processing continues

rules.rule_name: Merchant Zip Code Validation
rules.rule_description: The Merchant Zip Code is a mandatory field that must be provided before the transaction can be added.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
27: Merchant Zip Validation
Verify not empty

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Merchant City has been successfully validated
acceptance_criteria.When: The Merchant Zip Code field (MZIPI) is evaluated during data field validation
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the Merchant Zip Code field is empty (spaces or LOW-VALUES), the error flag is set to 'Y', the message 'Merchant Zip can NOT be empty...' is displayed, the cursor is positioned on the Merchant Zip field, and the screen is redisplayed; if the Merchant Zip Code field contains a value, processing continues to the confirmation check

rules.rule_name: Transaction Add Confirmation Check
rules.rule_description: Before a transaction is permanently added, the user must explicitly confirm the action by entering Y. Entering N or leaving the field blank prompts the user to confirm. Any other value is treated as invalid.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
28: Confirmation Check
User confirmed Y/N?

acceptance_criteria.Given: All input key fields and data fields have passed validation
acceptance_criteria.When: The Confirm field (CONFIRMI) value is evaluated
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the Confirm field contains 'Y' or 'y', the transaction addition process is invoked; if the Confirm field contains 'N', 'n', spaces, or LOW-VALUES, the error flag is set to 'Y', the message 'Confirm to add this transaction...' is displayed, the cursor is positioned on the Confirm field, and the screen is redisplayed prompting the user to confirm; if the Confirm field contains any other value, the error flag is set to 'Y', the message 'Invalid value. Valid values are (Y/N)...' is displayed, the cursor is positioned on the Confirm field, and the screen is redisplayed

rules.rule_name: New Transaction ID Generation
rules.rule_description: The system automatically generates a unique Transaction ID by retrieving the highest existing Transaction ID from the transaction file and incrementing it by 1.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
29: New Transaction ID Generation
Browse transaction file backwards
Increment last ID by 1

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has confirmed the transaction addition with 'Y'
acceptance_criteria.When: The system generates a new Transaction ID
acceptance_criteria.Then: The transaction file is browsed starting from the highest possible key value (HIGH-VALUES) in reverse order to retrieve the last (highest) existing Transaction ID; the browse is then ended; the retrieved Transaction ID is incremented by 1 to produce the new unique Transaction ID for the transaction being added

rules.rule_name: Transaction Record Population
rules.rule_description: A new transaction record is assembled by populating all fields from the validated screen input and the auto-generated Transaction ID.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
30: Transaction Record Creation
Populate new transaction record
with all validated fields

acceptance_criteria.Given: A new Transaction ID has been generated
acceptance_criteria.When: The transaction record is being prepared for writing to the transaction file
acceptance_criteria.Then: The transaction record is initialized to empty values and then populated with: the auto-generated Transaction ID, Transaction Type Code (TTYPCDI), Transaction Category Code (TCATCDI), Transaction Source (TRNSRCI), Transaction Description (TDESCI), Transaction Amount converted to numeric (TRNAMTI), Card Number (CARDNINI), Merchant ID (MIDI), Merchant Name (MNAMEI), Merchant City (MCITYI), Merchant Zip (MZIPI), Original Date/Timestamp (TORIGDTI), and Processing Date/Timestamp (TPROCDTI)

rules.rule_name: Transaction Record Write and Outcome Handling
rules.rule_description: The fully populated transaction record is written to the transaction file, and the outcome determines whether a success or error message is presented to the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
31: Transaction Record Write
Write new transaction to file

acceptance_criteria.Given: The transaction record has been fully populated with all validated field values
acceptance_criteria.When: The system writes the new transaction record to the transaction file (TRANSACT)
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the write is successful, all input fields are cleared, a success message in green is displayed reading 'Transaction added successfully. Your Tran ID is [new Transaction ID].', and the screen is redisplayed for new entry; if the write fails due to a duplicate Transaction ID, the error flag is set to 'Y', the message 'Tran ID already exist...' is displayed, the cursor is positioned on the Account ID field, and the screen is redisplayed; if the write fails for any other reason, the error flag is set to 'Y', the message 'Unable to Add Transaction...' is displayed, the cursor is positioned on the Account ID field, and the screen is redisplayed

rules.rule_name: Screen Header Population
rules.rule_description: Before displaying the Add Transaction screen, the header area is populated with current system information including titles, program identity, current date, and current time.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
33: Screen Header Population
Populate title, program name,
transaction ID, date, time

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Add Transaction screen is about to be sent to the user terminal
acceptance_criteria.When: The screen header population routine is executed
acceptance_criteria.Then: The screen header is populated with: the application title line 1 (CCDA-TITLE01), the application title line 2 (CCDA-TITLE02), the current transaction ID (WS-TRANID), the current program name (WS-PGMNAME), the current date formatted as MM/DD/YY, and the current time formatted as HH:MM:SS

rules.rule_name: Add Transaction Screen Display
rules.rule_description: The Add Transaction screen is sent to the user terminal with all current field values, the current message (error or status), and the cursor positioned on the relevant field.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
34: Add Transaction Screen Display
Send screen to user terminal
with validation/status messages

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen header has been populated and a message (error or status) has been set in WS-MESSAGE
acceptance_criteria.When: The system sends the Add Transaction screen to the user terminal
acceptance_criteria.Then: The message from WS-MESSAGE is moved to the screen error message output field (ERRMSGO), the screen map COTRN2A from mapset COTRN02 is sent to the terminal with the ERASE option to clear the previous screen and the CURSOR option to position the cursor on the designated field; the program then returns control to CICS awaiting the next user interaction, passing the current transaction ID and communication area

rules.rule_name: Data Fields Cleared on Key Field Validation Error
rules.rule_description: When a key field validation error (Account ID or Card Number) has occurred, all transaction data fields are cleared from the screen to prevent processing of potentially mismatched data.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
15: Transaction Type Code Validation
Verify not empty and numeric

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is beginning data field validation after key field validation
acceptance_criteria.When: The error flag is already set to ON (indicating a prior key field validation failure)
acceptance_criteria.Then: All transaction data input fields are cleared to spaces: Transaction Type Code (TTYPCDI), Transaction Category Code (TCATCDI), Transaction Source (TRNSRCI), Transaction Amount (TRNAMTI), Transaction Description (TDESCI), Origination Date (TORIGDTI), Processing Date (TPROCDTI), Merchant ID (MIDI), Merchant Name (MNAMEI), Merchant City (MCITYI), and Merchant Zip (MZIPI)

rules.rule_name: Reset Error Flag at Program Start
rules.rule_description: At the beginning of every program invocation for the Add Transaction screen, the error flag must be reset to its default OFF state to ensure no residual error state from a previous interaction affects the current processing cycle.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Reset Error Flag
Set to OFF

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Add Transaction program (COTRN2AC) has been invoked for any reason, including initial entry, re-entry after user input, or navigation from another screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The program begins execution at the start of the main processing paragraph (MAIN-PARA)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The error flag (ERR-FLG) must be set to OFF (ERR-FLG-OFF = TRUE), ensuring no prior error condition carries forward into the current processing cycle

rules.rule_name: Reset User-Modified Flag at Program Start
rules.rule_description: At the beginning of every program invocation for the Add Transaction screen, the user-modified indicator must be reset to NO to ensure the system correctly tracks whether the user has made any changes during the current interaction.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Reset User-Modified Flag
Set to NO

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Add Transaction program (COTRN2AC) has been invoked for any reason, including initial entry, re-entry after user input, or navigation from another screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The program begins execution immediately after the error flag has been reset
acceptance_criteria.Then: The user-modified flag (USR-MODIFIED) must be set to NO (USR-MODIFIED-NO = TRUE), indicating that no user modifications have been detected yet in the current processing cycle

rules.rule_name: Clear Working Message Field at Program Start
rules.rule_description: At the beginning of every program invocation for the Add Transaction screen, the internal working message field must be cleared to spaces to ensure no residual message text from a previous interaction is inadvertently displayed or processed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Clear Message Fields
Set Working Message to Spaces
Set Screen Error Message to Spaces

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Add Transaction program (COTRN2AC) has been invoked for any reason, including initial entry, re-entry after user input, or navigation from another screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The program begins execution immediately after the user-modified flag has been reset
acceptance_criteria.Then: The internal working message field (WS-MESSAGE) must be set to spaces (blank), removing any message text that may have been set during a prior program invocation or interaction

rules.rule_name: Clear Screen Error Message Field at Program Start
rules.rule_description: At the beginning of every program invocation for the Add Transaction screen, the error message field displayed on the screen must be cleared to spaces to ensure no stale error message from a previous interaction remains visible to the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Clear Message Fields
Set Working Message to Spaces
Set Screen Error Message to Spaces

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Add Transaction program (COTRN2AC) has been invoked for any reason, including initial entry, re-entry after user input, or navigation from another screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The program begins execution immediately after the working message field has been cleared
acceptance_criteria.Then: The screen-displayed error message field (ERRMSGO on screen map COTRN2AO) must be set to spaces (blank), ensuring the user does not see any error message carried over from a previous screen interaction

key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:

rules.rule_name: Detect Unauthenticated or Direct Access Attempt
rules.rule_description: When a user accesses the Add Transaction screen without an active session (i.e., no communication area data is present), the system identifies this as an unauthenticated or direct access attempt and initiates a redirect to the Sign-On screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is this a New/Direct Access? No Session Data Present

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user attempts to access the Add Transaction screen (program COTRN2AC)
acceptance_criteria.When: The session communication area length (EIBCALEN) equals zero, indicating no active session data or communication context is present
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system identifies the user as unauthenticated with no active session, and proceeds to redirect the user to the Sign-On screen

rules.rule_name: Set Sign-On Screen as Redirect Destination for Unauthenticated Access
rules.rule_description: When no active session is detected, the system sets the target destination program to the Sign-On screen (COSGN00C) so that the user can be properly authenticated before accessing the Add Transaction functionality.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Destination to Sign-On Screen COSGN00C

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has determined that the user has no active session (EIBCALEN equals zero)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares to redirect the unauthenticated user
acceptance_criteria.Then: The destination program is set to the Sign-On screen identified as 'COSGN00C', which will be used as the target for the redirect

rules.rule_name: Record Current Program and Transaction Context Before Redirect
rules.rule_description: Before redirecting the user to the Sign-On screen, the system captures and stores the current transaction identifier and program name as the originating context. This allows the Sign-On screen and subsequent navigation to know where the user came from, enabling a potential return to this screen after successful authentication.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Record Current Program and Transaction Details for Return Navigation

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has determined the user must be redirected to the Sign-On screen due to no active session
acceptance_criteria.When: The system is preparing the navigation context before executing the redirect
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system records the current transaction identifier (WS-TRANID) into the 'from transaction' field (CDEMO-FROM-TRANID), records the current program name (WS-PGMNAME) into the 'from program' field (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM), and resets the program context indicator (CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT) to zero to indicate a fresh navigation state

rules.rule_name: Redirect Unauthenticated User to Sign-On Screen
rules.rule_description: After recording the navigation context, the system transfers control to the Sign-On screen (COSGN00C), passing along the communication area that contains the recorded navigation details. This ensures the user must authenticate before being able to add a transaction.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Redirect User to Sign-On Screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: The destination has been set to the Sign-On screen (COSGN00C) and the current program and transaction context have been recorded in the communication area
acceptance_criteria.When: The system executes the redirect
acceptance_criteria.Then: Control is transferred to the Sign-On screen program (COSGN00C) along with the full communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) containing the originating program name and transaction identifier, so that the user is presented with the Sign-On screen and the system retains the return navigation path

rules.rule_name: Detect and Mark First-Time Program Entry
rules.rule_description: When a user accesses the Add Transaction screen for the first time in a session (the program has not been re-entered), the system must identify this as an initial entry and immediately mark the session so that subsequent visits are treated as returning entries, preventing repeated initialization.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: First-Time Entry Detected

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user navigates to the Add Transaction screen and the program context indicates this is NOT a re-entry (the re-enterable flag is not yet set in the communication area)
acceptance_criteria.When: The program evaluates the session state at the start of processing
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program identifies this as a first-time entry and immediately sets the re-enterable flag to TRUE in the communication area, so that all future visits to this screen within the same session are recognized as returning entries and bypass the initialization logic

rules.rule_name: Initialize Add Transaction Screen on First Entry
rules.rule_description: On the first visit to the Add Transaction screen, all screen output fields must be cleared to their lowest values and the cursor must be positioned at the Account ID input field, ensuring the user starts with a completely blank form.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Initialize Add Transaction Screen
Clear all screen fields

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has confirmed this is a first-time entry to the Add Transaction screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The screen initialization process begins
acceptance_criteria.Then: All output fields on the Add Transaction screen (COTRN2AO) are cleared to LOW-VALUES (blank/reset state), and the cursor is positioned at the Account ID field (ACTIDINL set to -1) so the user can begin entering transaction details from a clean form

rules.rule_name: Determine Whether a Card Number Was Passed from a Prior Screen
rules.rule_description: After initializing the screen, the system must check whether the user arrived at the Add Transaction screen with a pre-selected Card Number carried over from a prior screen. This determines whether the screen should be pre-populated or displayed blank.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Was a Card Number
passed from
prior screen?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Add Transaction screen has been initialized and the communication area contains context from the prior screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the pre-selected transaction value (CDEMO-CT02-TRN-SELECTED) in the communication area
acceptance_criteria.Then: If CDEMO-CT02-TRN-SELECTED contains a value that is neither SPACES nor LOW-VALUES, the system determines that a Card Number was passed from the prior screen and proceeds to pre-populate the Card Number field; otherwise, if CDEMO-CT02-TRN-SELECTED is SPACES or LOW-VALUES, the system determines no prior selection was made and displays a blank Add Transaction screen

rules.rule_name: Pre-Populate Card Number from Prior Screen Selection
rules.rule_description: When a Card Number has been passed from a prior screen, the system must automatically populate the Card Number input field on the Add Transaction screen with the value carried over, so the user does not need to re-enter it.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Pre-populate Card Number
on the screen
from prior selection

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has determined that a Card Number value (CDEMO-CT02-TRN-SELECTED) was passed from the prior screen and is not blank or empty
acceptance_criteria.When: The pre-population step executes
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Card Number input field (CARDNINI of COTRN2AI) on the Add Transaction screen is populated with the value from CDEMO-CT02-TRN-SELECTED, making it available for immediate processing and display to the user

rules.rule_name: Retrieve Associated Account ID for Pre-Populated Card Number
rules.rule_description: After the Card Number is pre-populated from the prior screen, the system must immediately process it through the full Enter key processing logic to validate the Card Number, look up the associated Account ID from the card cross-reference, and populate the Account ID field — ensuring the screen is fully resolved before being displayed to the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Process the pre-populated
Card Number to retrieve
associated Account ID

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Card Number input field (CARDNINI of COTRN2AI) has been pre-populated with a value passed from the prior screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The system invokes the PROCESS-ENTER-KEY routine
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system executes the full Enter key processing flow, which includes: (1) validating the Card Number is numeric, (2) looking up the Card Number in the card cross-reference file to retrieve the associated Account ID, (3) populating the Account ID field (ACTIDINI of COTRN2AI) with the retrieved value, and (4) proceeding through data field validation and confirmation checks — displaying the Add Transaction screen with both Card Number and Account ID populated, or showing an appropriate error message if the Card Number is invalid or not found

rules.rule_name: Display Blank Add Transaction Screen When No Prior Selection Exists
rules.rule_description: When the user navigates directly to the Add Transaction screen without a prior Card Number selection, the system must display a fully blank Add Transaction screen with the cursor on the Account ID field, prompting the user to enter either an Account ID or Card Number to begin.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Display blank
Add Transaction Screen
with no pre-population

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Add Transaction screen has been initialized, the cursor is set to the Account ID field, and no Card Number was passed from a prior screen (CDEMO-CT02-TRN-SELECTED is SPACES or LOW-VALUES)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system invokes the SEND-TRNADD-SCREEN routine
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Add Transaction screen (map COTRN2A from mapset COTRN02) is displayed to the user with all input fields blank, the header populated with current date, time, transaction ID, and program name, no error messages shown, and the cursor positioned at the Account ID field — awaiting the user's input

rules.rule_name: Display Add Transaction Screen with Pre-Populated Card Number and Account ID
rules.rule_description: After the pre-populated Card Number has been processed and the associated Account ID has been retrieved, the system displays the Add Transaction screen showing both the Card Number and Account ID fields populated, ready for the user to complete the remaining transaction details.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Display Add Transaction Screen
with Card Number
pre-populated

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Card Number pre-populated from the prior screen has been successfully validated and processed through PROCESS-ENTER-KEY, and the associated Account ID has been retrieved from the card cross-reference
acceptance_criteria.When: The SEND-TRNADD-SCREEN routine is invoked as part of the PROCESS-ENTER-KEY flow
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Add Transaction screen (map COTRN2A from mapset COTRN02) is displayed with the Card Number field (CARDNINI) and Account ID field (ACTIDINI) both populated with their respective values, the header showing current date, time, transaction ID, and program name, and any relevant validation messages or confirmation prompts shown — allowing the user to proceed with entering the remaining transaction details

rules.rule_name: Identify Returning User Session for Add Transaction Screen
rules.rule_description: Determines whether the user is returning to the Add Transaction screen (i.e., has already visited it at least once in the current session) by checking the program re-entry flag in the communication area, and routes them to the screen input reception flow.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Returning User Visits
Add Transaction Screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user accesses the Add Transaction screen and a valid communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) exists from a prior interaction (EIBCALEN is not zero), and the program re-entry flag (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER) is already set to TRUE indicating the user has visited this screen before
acceptance_criteria.When: The program evaluates the re-entry flag from the loaded communication area
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program identifies this as a returning user visit and proceeds to receive and process the user's screen input, bypassing the first-time initialization logic (screen clearing, cursor positioning, and pre-population)

rules.rule_name: Receive User Input from Add Transaction Screen
rules.rule_description: Captures all field values entered by the user on the Add Transaction screen (COTRN2A in mapset COTRN02), including Account ID, Card Number, transaction details, merchant information, dates, amount, and the confirmation indicator, making them available for subsequent processing.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Receive User Input
from Add Transaction Screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: A returning user has submitted the Add Transaction screen (COTRN2A / COTRN02) by pressing a function key
acceptance_criteria.When: The system receives the screen input
acceptance_criteria.Then: All field values entered by the user on the Add Transaction screen are captured into the input map (COTRN2AI), including Account ID, Card Number, Transaction Type Code, Category Code, Source, Description, Amount, Original Date, Processing Date, Merchant ID, Merchant Name, Merchant City, Merchant Zip, and Confirmation indicator, making them available for key evaluation and business processing

rules.rule_name: Evaluate Function Key to Determine Processing Route
rules.rule_description: After receiving screen input, the system evaluates which function key the user pressed (EIBAID) to determine the appropriate processing path: Enter for transaction submission, PF3 for back navigation, PF4 for screen clear, PF5 for copying the last transaction, or any other key triggers an invalid key error.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Evaluate
Function Key Pressed

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has submitted the Add Transaction screen and all field inputs have been received into COTRN2AI
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the function key identifier (EIBAID) pressed by the user
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system routes processing as follows: if ENTER key (DFHENTER) was pressed, route to Enter Key Processing; if PF3 (DFHPF3) was pressed, route to Navigate Back; if PF4 (DFHPF4) was pressed, route to Clear Screen; if PF5 (DFHPF5) was pressed, route to Copy Last Transaction; if any other key was pressed, route to Invalid Key Handling

rules.rule_name: Route to Enter Key Processing for Transaction Submission
rules.rule_description: When the user presses the Enter key on the Add Transaction screen, the system routes control to the Enter Key Processing routine, which performs input validation and, upon confirmation, adds the transaction.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Route to
Enter Key Processing

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has filled in transaction details on the Add Transaction screen and the screen input has been received
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses the Enter key (DFHENTER)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system invokes the Enter Key Processing routine (PROCESS-ENTER-KEY), which will validate all input fields and, if valid and confirmed, add the transaction to the system

rules.rule_name: Route to Navigate Back to Previous Screen via PF3
rules.rule_description: When the user presses PF3 on the Add Transaction screen, the system navigates back to the originating program. If no originating program is recorded in the session, the system defaults to the main menu (COMEN01C).
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Route to
Navigate Back

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the Add Transaction screen and the screen input has been received
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses PF3 (DFHPF3)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system checks the originating program stored in the communication area (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM): if CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM contains a valid program name (not spaces or low-values), that program name is set as the navigation target (CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM); if CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM is spaces or low-values, the navigation target defaults to the main menu program 'COMEN01C'; the system then transfers control to the determined target program, passing the current session communication area

rules.rule_name: Route to Clear Screen via PF4
rules.rule_description: When the user presses PF4 on the Add Transaction screen, the system clears all input fields on the screen, allowing the user to start a fresh transaction entry.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Route to
Clear Screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the Add Transaction screen and the screen input has been received
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses PF4 (DFHPF4)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system invokes the Clear Current Screen routine (CLEAR-CURRENT-SCREEN), which resets all input fields to spaces (Account ID, Card Number, Type Code, Category Code, Source, Amount, Description, Original Date, Processing Date, Merchant ID, Merchant Name, Merchant City, Merchant Zip, and Confirmation), positions the cursor on the Account ID field, clears any existing messages, and redisplays the blank Add Transaction screen

rules.rule_name: Route to Copy Last Transaction Data via PF5
rules.rule_description: When the user presses PF5 on the Add Transaction screen, the system retrieves the most recently added transaction's details and pre-populates the screen fields, allowing the user to reuse transaction data as a template for a new entry.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Route to
Copy Last Transaction

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the Add Transaction screen, has entered a valid Account ID or Card Number, and the screen input has been received
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses PF5 (DFHPF5)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system invokes the Copy Last Transaction Data routine (COPY-LAST-TRAN-DATA), which first validates the Account ID or Card Number key fields, then retrieves the last transaction record from the transaction file, and if no key field errors exist, copies the following fields from the last transaction into the screen: Transaction Type Code, Category Code, Source, Amount (formatted), Description, Original Date, Processing Date, Merchant ID, Merchant Name, Merchant City, and Merchant Zip; the system then proceeds to Enter Key Processing to validate the pre-populated data and prompt for confirmation

rules.rule_name: Handle Invalid Function Key Press
rules.rule_description: When the user presses any function key other than Enter, PF3, PF4, or PF5 on the Add Transaction screen, the system sets an error condition and displays an invalid key message, redisplaying the screen without processing any input.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Route to
Invalid Key Handling

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the Add Transaction screen and the screen input has been received
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses any key other than Enter (DFHENTER), PF3 (DFHPF3), PF4 (DFHPF4), or PF5 (DFHPF5)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to 'Y' (WS-ERR-FLG), populates the error message with the standard invalid key message (CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY) into WS-MESSAGE, and redisplays the Add Transaction screen with the error message shown, without performing any transaction processing or field validation

key_functionalities.title: Enter Key Processing
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    START([Enter Key Pressed])
    V1[Validate Account ID\nor Card Number Fields]
    V2[Validate All Transaction\nData Fields]
    CONF{Check Confirmation\nField Value}

rules.rule_name: Determine Navigation Destination on PF3 Press
rules.rule_description: When the user presses PF3 to navigate back, the system determines the correct destination program. If the screen was invoked from a known calling program, that program is set as the destination. If no calling program is recorded, the default main menu (COMEN01C) is used as the destination.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Was this screen called from another program?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the Add Transaction screen and the communication area contains the calling program identifier (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM)
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses PF3 to navigate back
acceptance_criteria.Then: If CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM contains a valid program name (not spaces or low-values), the destination program (CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM) is set to that calling program name; otherwise, the destination is set to the default main menu program 'COMEN01C'

rules.rule_name: Fallback to Sign-On Screen When Destination Is Still Invalid
rules.rule_description: As a safety measure, after the destination program has been determined, if the destination program identifier is still empty or unset (low-values or spaces), the system overrides it and redirects the user to the Sign-On screen (COSGN00C) to ensure navigation never fails.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Destination Still Empty

acceptance_criteria.Given: The navigation destination program (CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM) has been evaluated after PF3 was pressed
acceptance_criteria.When: The destination program identifier is still empty (spaces or low-values) after the initial determination step
acceptance_criteria.Then: The destination program is overridden and set to the Sign-On screen program 'COSGN00C', ensuring the user is always redirected to a valid screen

rules.rule_name: Record Current Program Context in Communication Area Before Navigation
rules.rule_description: Before transferring control to the destination program, the system records the current program's identity and the current transaction ID into the communication area, and resets the program context indicator to zero. This allows the destination program to know which program initiated the navigation and to maintain session continuity.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Record Current Program and Transaction ID in Communication Area

acceptance_criteria.Given: The destination program has been determined and the system is about to transfer control away from the Add Transaction screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The navigation back action is being executed
acceptance_criteria.Then: The current transaction ID (WS-TRANID) is recorded as the originating transaction ID (CDEMO-FROM-TRANID) in the communication area, the current program name (WS-PGMNAME) is recorded as the originating program (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM) in the communication area, and the program context indicator (CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT) is reset to zero

rules.rule_name: Transfer Control to Destination Program with Communication Area
rules.rule_description: The system transfers control to the determined destination program, passing the full communication area so that session state, user context, and navigation history are preserved across the program transition.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Transfer Control to Destination Program passing Communication Area

acceptance_criteria.Given: The destination program has been validated and set in CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM, and the communication area has been updated with the current program context
acceptance_criteria.When: The system executes the navigation transfer
acceptance_criteria.Then: Control is transferred to the destination program identified in CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM, and the full communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) is passed to the destination program to maintain session continuity

acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses any function key other than Enter, PF3, PF4, or PF5

rules.rule_name: Load Standard Invalid Key Error Message

rules.rule_name: Redisplay Add Transaction Screen with Invalid Key Error Message
rules.rule_description: After detecting an invalid key press and loading the error message, the system must redisplay the Add Transaction screen to the user with the error message visible, the current date and time in the header, and the screen awaiting the next valid user action.

rules.rule_name: Account ID Numeric Format Validation

rules.rule_name: Account ID Non-Numeric Error Display

rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display Error Message: 'Account ID must be Numeric'

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has entered a non-numeric value in the Account ID field on the Add Transaction screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The system detects that the Account ID is not numeric
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system marks the transaction entry session as having an error, displays the message 'Account ID must be Numeric...' in the screen message area, sets the cursor focus to the Account ID input field, and redisplays the Add Transaction screen so the user can correct the value

rules.rule_name: Account ID Conversion to Numeric Format
rules.rule_description: Once the Account ID passes the numeric character check, it is converted from its display string format into a pure numeric value and stored back into the Account ID field in a standardized numeric format for consistent processing and lookup.

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has entered a valid numeric Account ID on the Add Transaction screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The Account ID passes the numeric character validation
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system converts the Account ID string to its numeric equivalent using a numeric value function and stores the converted numeric value back into the Account ID field in a standardized format, ready for cross-reference lookup

rules.rule_name: Account ID Cross-Reference Lookup Invocation

acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the Account ID as the lookup key, invokes the Account-to-Card cross-reference lookup process, and upon a successful lookup, automatically populates the Card Number field on the Add Transaction screen with the Card Number associated with the given Account ID

rules.rule_name: Account ID Not Found in Cross-Reference File

rules.rule_name: Account ID Cross-Reference Lookup System Failure

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has performed a lookup of the entered Account ID in the Card-Account Cross-Reference Index file (CXACAIX)
acceptance_criteria.When: The lookup encounters an unexpected failure condition (neither a successful retrieval nor a standard 'not found' response)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to 'Y', displays the error message 'Unable to lookup Acct in XREF AIX file...' on the screen, positions the cursor on the Account ID input field to highlight it for correction, and returns the Add Transaction screen to the user for correction

rules.rule_name: Auto-Populate Card Number from Account Cross-Reference

acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to 'Y', displays the error message 'Card Number must be Numeric...' on the Add Transaction screen, positions the cursor on the Card Number field, and halts further processing awaiting user correction

rules.rule_name: Card Number Cross-Reference Lookup to Retrieve Account ID

rules.rule_name: Account ID Auto-Populated from Card Number Cross-Reference

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has entered a valid Card Number on the Add Transaction screen, and the system has successfully located the Card Number in the Card Cross-Reference file (CCXREF)

rules.rule_name: Card Number Not Found in Cross-Reference

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has entered a Card Number on the Add Transaction screen, the Card Number has been validated as numeric and converted, and the system has performed a lookup in the Card Cross-Reference file (CCXREF)

rules.rule_name: Card Number Lookup System Failure

rules.rule_name: Accept Origination Date When Validation Succeeds With No Errors

acceptance_criteria.Given: The external date validation utility CSUTLDTC has been called with the user-entered Origination Date and the expected date format
acceptance_criteria.When: The validation utility returns a severity code of '0000', indicating the date passed all calendar checks with no errors
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Origination Date is accepted as a valid calendar date, no error flag is set, no error message is displayed, and processing continues to the next validation step

rules.rule_name: Accept Origination Date When Validation Result Is a Warning Only (Message 2513)
rules.rule_description: If the date validation utility returns a non-success result but the specific message number is 2513 (which represents a warning-only condition, not a hard error), the Origination Date is still accepted and processing continues without displaying an error to the user.

acceptance_criteria.Given: The external date validation utility CSUTLDTC has been called with the user-entered Origination Date, and the utility has returned a result with a severity code other than '0000' (i.e., validation did not fully succeed)

acceptance_criteria.Then: The Origination Date is accepted despite the non-success severity code, no error flag is set, no error message is displayed, and processing continues to the next validation step

rules.rule_name: Reject Origination Date and Display Error When Validation Fails With a Hard Error

acceptance_criteria.Then: The error flag is set to 'Y', the error message 'Orig Date - Not a valid date...' is stored and displayed on the Add Transaction screen, the cursor is positioned on the Origination Date field to prompt correction, and the Add Transaction screen is redisplayed to the user — halting further processing until the error is resolved

acceptance_criteria.Given: The search position has been set to the highest possible value and the system needs to find the last used Transaction ID

rules.rule_name: Handle Transaction File Browse Open Failure

rules.rule_name: Read Last Transaction Record to Retrieve Highest Transaction ID

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction File has been successfully opened for backward browsing from the highest key position

acceptance_criteria.Then: The last used Transaction ID is successfully retrieved from the most recent transaction record in the file, and this value is stored for use in generating the next Transaction ID

rules.rule_name: Handle Empty Transaction File During ID Generation
rules.rule_description: If the Transaction File contains no records (end of file is reached immediately during backward browse), the system must treat the last used Transaction ID as zero, so that the first transaction will be assigned Transaction ID 1.

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction File has been successfully opened for backward browsing and the system attempts to read the last transaction record
acceptance_criteria.When: The backward read reaches the end of file, indicating that no transaction records exist in the Transaction File
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Transaction ID is set to zero (0) as the baseline, so that when incremented by 1, the first transaction in the system will be assigned Transaction ID 1

rules.rule_name: Handle Transaction Record Read Failure During ID Generation

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction File has been successfully opened for backward browsing and the system attempts to read the last transaction record

acceptance_criteria.Then: The error flag is set to indicate a failure, the message 'Unable to lookup Transaction...' is displayed to the user, the cursor is positioned on the Account ID field, and the Add Transaction screen is redisplayed — preventing the transaction from being added

rules.rule_name: Close Transaction File Browse After ID Retrieval
rules.rule_description: After the last Transaction ID has been retrieved (or determined to be zero for an empty file), the Transaction File browse session must be closed before proceeding to generate the new Transaction ID.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Close the Transaction File Browse

acceptance_criteria.Given: The backward browse of the Transaction File has completed, either by successfully reading the last transaction record or by determining the file is empty
acceptance_criteria.When: The system closes the Transaction File browse session
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Transaction File browse is terminated and the system proceeds to calculate the new unique Transaction ID based on the retrieved last Transaction ID value

rules.rule_name: Generate New Unique Transaction ID by Incrementing Last Used ID
rules.rule_description: The system generates a new unique Transaction ID by taking the last used Transaction ID retrieved from the Transaction File and incrementing it by exactly 1. This ensures sequential, unique Transaction IDs are assigned to each new transaction.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Increment last Transaction ID by 1 to generate new unique Transaction ID

acceptance_criteria.Given: The last used Transaction ID has been successfully retrieved from the Transaction File (or set to zero if the file was empty) and the Transaction File browse has been closed
acceptance_criteria.When: The system calculates the new Transaction ID
acceptance_criteria.Then: The new Transaction ID is computed as the last used Transaction ID plus 1 (Last Transaction ID + 1), producing a sequentially unique identifier that will be assigned to the new transaction record being added
