Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the Origination Date format and characters at positions 9 and 10 (the day portion DD) of the Origination Date are not all numeric digits
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to 'Y', displays the error message 'Orig Date should be in format YYYY-MM-DD', positions the cursor on the Origination Date field, and redisplays the Add Transaction screen with the error message — preventing any further validation or transaction processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Origination Date Day (DD) Component Must Be Numeric
all_rules.Rule_Description: Validates that characters 9 and 10 of the Origination Date, representing the day (DD), are numeric digits as required by the YYYY-MM-DD date format standard. This is the final structural format check before the date is considered structurally valid.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has entered a value in the Origination Date field on the Add Transaction screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Origination Date field is non-empty AND positions 1-4 are numeric (YYYY) AND position 5 is a hyphen AND positions 6-7 are numeric (MM) AND position 8 is a hyphen AND positions 9-10 are numeric (DD)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: No error is raised for the Origination Date format, the error flag remains unchanged, no error message is set for this validation, and the system proceeds to the next validation step (calendar date validity check)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Origination Date Format Fully Valid — Proceed to Next Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Confirms that the Origination Date has passed all structural format checks (non-empty, YYYY numeric, first hyphen, MM numeric, second hyphen, DD numeric) and allows the transaction add process to continue to the next validation step.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Add Transaction screen and has entered values for Account ID or Card Number and other transaction fields
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user submits the transaction form and the Processing Date field is empty, blank (spaces), or contains only low values
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) set the error flag to 'Y', (2) display the error message 'Proc Date can NOT be empty...', (3) position the cursor on the Processing Date field, and (4) redisplay the Add Transaction screen awaiting user correction — no further validation is performed for this submission

all_rules.Rule_Name: Processing Date Mandatory Field Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Ensures that the Processing Date field is not left empty or blank when submitting a new transaction. The Processing Date is a required field and must contain a value before the transaction can proceed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Add Transaction screen and the Processing Date field contains a non-empty value
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the Processing Date and the first 4 characters (positions 1 through 4) are not numeric
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) set the error flag to 'Y', (2) display the error message 'Proc Date should be in format YYYY-MM-DD', (3) position the cursor on the Processing Date field, and (4) redisplay the Add Transaction screen awaiting user correction — no further validation is performed for this submission

all_rules.Rule_Name: Processing Date Year Component Format Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Validates that the first four characters of the Processing Date represent a numeric year component (YYYY) as required by the YYYY-MM-DD date format standard.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Add Transaction screen, the Processing Date field contains a non-empty value, and the first 4 characters (year) are numeric
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the Processing Date and the 5th character (position 5, length 1) is not equal to a hyphen '-'
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) set the error flag to 'Y', (2) display the error message 'Proc Date should be in format YYYY-MM-DD', (3) position the cursor on the Processing Date field, and (4) redisplay the Add Transaction screen awaiting user correction — no further validation is performed for this submission

all_rules.Rule_Name: Processing Date First Separator Hyphen Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Validates that the 5th character of the Processing Date is a hyphen (-) separator between the year and month components, as required by the YYYY-MM-DD date format standard.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Add Transaction screen, the Processing Date field contains a non-empty value, the first 4 characters (year) are numeric, and the 5th character is a hyphen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the Processing Date and the 6th and 7th characters (positions 6 through 7, length 2) are not numeric
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) set the error flag to 'Y', (2) display the error message 'Proc Date should be in format YYYY-MM-DD', (3) position the cursor on the Processing Date field, and (4) redisplay the Add Transaction screen awaiting user correction — no further validation is performed for this submission

all_rules.Rule_Name: Processing Date Month Component Format Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Validates that the 6th and 7th characters of the Processing Date represent a numeric month component (MM) as required by the YYYY-MM-DD date format standard.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Add Transaction screen, the Processing Date field contains a non-empty value, the first 4 characters (year) are numeric, the 5th character is a hyphen, and the 6th and 7th characters (month) are numeric
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the Processing Date and the 8th character (position 8, length 1) is not equal to a hyphen '-'
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) set the error flag to 'Y', (2) display the error message 'Proc Date should be in format YYYY-MM-DD', (3) position the cursor on the Processing Date field, and (4) redisplay the Add Transaction screen awaiting user correction — no further validation is performed for this submission

all_rules.Rule_Name: Processing Date Second Separator Hyphen Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Validates that the 8th character of the Processing Date is a hyphen (-) separator between the month and day components, as required by the YYYY-MM-DD date format standard.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Add Transaction screen, the Processing Date field contains a non-empty value, the first 4 characters (year) are numeric, the 5th character is a hyphen, the 6th and 7th characters (month) are numeric, and the 8th character is a hyphen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the Processing Date and the 9th and 10th characters (positions 9 through 10, length 2) are not numeric
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) set the error flag to 'Y', (2) display the error message 'Proc Date should be in format YYYY-MM-DD', (3) position the cursor on the Processing Date field, and (4) redisplay the Add Transaction screen awaiting user correction — no further validation is performed for this submission; if all five structural checks pass, the Processing Date format is considered valid and processing continues to the next validation step

all_rules.Rule_Name: Processing Date Day Component Format Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Validates that the 9th and 10th characters of the Processing Date represent a numeric day component (DD) as required by the YYYY-MM-DD date format standard. When all five structural checks pass, the Processing Date format is considered valid.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has entered an Origination Date on the Add Transaction screen that has passed format validation (YYYY-MM-DD structure check), and the system is proceeding to calendar-level validation
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the Origination Date value and the expected date format, clears any prior validation result, and calls the external date validation utility CSUTLDTC passing the Origination Date, the date format, and a result container
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The date validation utility CSUTLDTC is invoked with the Origination Date and its format, and the validation result (including severity code and message number) is returned and stored for evaluation in the next step

all_rules.Rule_Name: Submit Origination Date to Calendar Validation Utility
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before accepting the Origination Date entered by the user, the system must invoke the external date validation utility (CSUTLDTC) to verify that the date is a legitimate calendar date. The date and its expected format are passed to the utility, and the result is captured for subsequent evaluation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The external date validation utility CSUTLDTC has been called with the user-entered Origination Date and the expected date format
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The validation utility returns a severity code of '0000', indicating the date passed all calendar checks with no errors
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Origination Date is accepted as a valid calendar date, no error flag is set, no error message is displayed, and processing continues to the next validation step

all_rules.Rule_Name: Accept Origination Date When Validation Succeeds With No Errors
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the date validation utility returns a successful result with no errors (severity code '0000'), the Origination Date is confirmed as a valid calendar date and processing continues to the next validation step without any error message.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The external date validation utility CSUTLDTC has been called with the user-entered Origination Date, and the utility has returned a result with a severity code other than '0000' (i.e., validation did not fully succeed)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The validation result message number is equal to '2513', indicating the condition is a warning only and not a hard calendar error
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Origination Date is accepted despite the non-success severity code, no error flag is set, no error message is displayed, and processing continues to the next validation step

all_rules.Rule_Name: Accept Origination Date When Validation Result Is a Warning Only (Message 2513)
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the date validation utility returns a non-success result but the specific message number is 2513 (which represents a warning-only condition, not a hard error), the Origination Date is still accepted and processing continues without displaying an error to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The external date validation utility CSUTLDTC has been called with the user-entered Origination Date, the utility has returned a result with a severity code other than '0000', and the result message number is NOT '2513'
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system determines the validation failure is a hard calendar error (not a warning), meaning the Origination Date does not represent a real, existing calendar date
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The error flag is set to 'Y', the error message 'Orig Date - Not a valid date...' is stored and displayed on the Add Transaction screen, the cursor is positioned on the Origination Date field to prompt correction, and the Add Transaction screen is redisplayed to the user — halting further processing until the error is resolved

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reject Origination Date and Display Error When Validation Fails With a Hard Error
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the date validation utility returns a non-success result and the message number is NOT 2513 (meaning it is a hard calendar error, not merely a warning), the Origination Date is rejected. An error flag is set, a specific error message is displayed to the user, the Origination Date field is highlighted for correction, and the Add Transaction screen is redisplayed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has entered a Processing Date on the Add Transaction screen, and the Processing Date has already passed format validation (YYYY-MM-DD structure check)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to perform calendar-level validation of the Processing Date
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must invoke the date validation utility (CSUTLDTC) by passing the Processing Date value and the configured date format as inputs, and capture the validation result for further evaluation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Submit Processing Date to Calendar Validation Utility
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user enters a Processing Date on the Add Transaction screen, the system must invoke the external date validation utility (CSUTLDTC) to verify that the date is a real calendar date, passing the Processing Date value and the expected date format as inputs.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The date validation utility (CSUTLDTC) has been called with the entered Processing Date and the configured date format
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The validation utility returns a severity code of '0000', indicating no errors were found
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Processing Date is accepted as a valid calendar date, no error message is displayed, and the system continues to the next validation step

all_rules.Rule_Name: Processing Date Accepted When Validation Utility Returns Success
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the date validation utility returns a severity code of '0000' (no errors), the Processing Date is confirmed as a valid calendar date and processing continues to the next validation step without any error message.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The date validation utility (CSUTLDTC) has been called with the entered Processing Date and the validation result is not a success (severity code is not '0000')
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The validation result message number equals '2513', indicating a warning-only condition
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Processing Date is treated as a valid calendar date, no error message is displayed, and the system continues to the next validation step without interruption

all_rules.Rule_Name: Processing Date Accepted When Validation Returns Warning Message 2513
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the date validation utility returns a non-success result but the specific message number is '2513', this is treated as a warning-only condition (not a hard error). The Processing Date is still considered valid and processing continues without displaying an error message.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The date validation utility (CSUTLDTC) has been called with the entered Processing Date, the validation result is not a success (severity code is not '0000'), and the result message number is NOT '2513'
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The validation utility confirms the Processing Date is not a real calendar date (hard error condition)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) set the error flag to 'Y', (2) display the error message 'Proc Date - Not a valid date...' on the screen, (3) position the cursor on the Processing Date input field to guide the user to correct the value, and (4) redisplay the Add Transaction screen with the error message — preventing any further processing until the error is resolved

all_rules.Rule_Name: Processing Date Rejected When Validation Returns a Hard Error
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the date validation utility returns a non-success result and the message number is anything other than '2513' (i.e., a hard error, not a warning), the Processing Date is rejected as an invalid calendar date. An error message is displayed, the Processing Date field is highlighted, and the user must correct the entry before proceeding.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Add Transaction screen and has entered valid Account ID or Card Number details
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user submits the transaction form with the Merchant ID field left empty or containing only blank spaces
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) Set the error flag to 'Y', (2) Display the error message 'Merchant ID can NOT be empty...' on the screen, (3) Position the cursor on the Merchant ID input field, and (4) Redisplay the Add Transaction screen so the user can correct the entry. The transaction must NOT be saved.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Merchant ID Mandatory Field Check
all_rules.Rule_Description: Ensures that the Merchant ID field is not left empty or blank when adding a new transaction. The Merchant ID is a required field and must be provided before the transaction can be processed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Add Transaction screen, has provided a non-empty Merchant ID value, and all prior validations (Account ID or Card Number, and all other mandatory data fields) have passed without errors
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user submits the transaction form with a Merchant ID that contains one or more non-numeric characters
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) Set the error flag to 'Y', (2) Display the error message 'Merchant ID must be Numeric...' on the screen, (3) Position the cursor on the Merchant ID input field, and (4) Redisplay the Add Transaction screen so the user can correct the entry. The transaction must NOT be saved.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Merchant ID Numeric Format Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Ensures that the Merchant ID field contains only numeric characters when adding a new transaction. A Merchant ID containing non-numeric characters (e.g., letters or special symbols) is considered invalid and must be rejected.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Add Transaction screen and has entered or is submitting transaction details, and the Merchant Name field contains only spaces or is completely empty (blank/low-values)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user submits the transaction form by pressing the Enter key, triggering the data field validation process
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) Set the error flag to 'Y' indicating a validation failure, (2) Set the error message to 'Merchant Name can NOT be empty...', (3) Position the cursor on the Merchant Name input field to guide the user to the error, (4) Redisplay the Add Transaction screen with the error message visible, so the user can correct the Merchant Name and resubmit

all_rules.Rule_Name: Merchant Name Mandatory Field Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Ensures that the Merchant Name field is not left empty or blank when a user submits the Add Transaction screen. This rule enforces that every transaction must have an associated Merchant Name before it can be processed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Merchant Name validation has failed because the Merchant Name field is empty or blank, the error flag has been set to 'Y', and the error message 'Merchant Name can NOT be empty...' has been prepared
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system invokes the screen display routine to send the Add Transaction screen back to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) Populate the screen header with current date, time, transaction ID, and program name, (2) Display the error message 'Merchant Name can NOT be empty...' in the error message area of the screen, (3) Render the Add Transaction screen (map COTRN2A from mapset COTRN02) with all previously entered field values retained and the cursor positioned on the Merchant Name field, (4) Maintain the active transaction session so the user can correct the input and resubmit without losing other entered data

all_rules.Rule_Name: Merchant Name Validation Error Screen Display
all_rules.Rule_Description: Defines the action taken when Merchant Name validation fails — the system must redisplay the Add Transaction screen with the error message and retain the current transaction session, allowing the user to correct the missing Merchant Name and resubmit.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Add Transaction screen and has entered data in the required fields up to and including Merchant Name, and the system has successfully passed all prior validations (Type Code, Category Code, Source, Description, Amount, Original Date, Processing Date, Merchant ID, and Merchant Name are all valid and non-empty)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user submits the screen and the Merchant City field is found to be empty (contains only spaces or no value at all)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) set the error indicator to 'Y' to flag a validation failure, (2) set the error message to 'Merchant City can NOT be empty...', (3) position the cursor on the Merchant City input field to direct the user's attention, and (4) redisplay the Add Transaction screen with the error message shown, requiring the user to provide a Merchant City value before the transaction can be saved

all_rules.Rule_Name: Merchant City Mandatory Field Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Validates that the Merchant City field is not left empty when a user submits the Add Transaction screen. If the Merchant City is missing, an error is raised, the field is highlighted, and the user is prompted to provide the value before the transaction can proceed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Merchant City validation has failed because the Merchant City field was found to be empty, the error flag has been set to 'Y', the error message 'Merchant City can NOT be empty...' has been set, and the cursor position has been directed to the Merchant City field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system triggers the display of the Add Transaction screen in response to the Merchant City validation error
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) populate the screen header with current date and time, transaction ID, and program name, (2) display the error message 'Merchant City can NOT be empty...' in the error message area of the screen, (3) render the Add Transaction screen with all previously entered field values retained, (4) position the cursor on the Merchant City field, and (5) await the user's next input action so they can supply the missing Merchant City value

all_rules.Rule_Name: Merchant City Validation - Error Screen Display
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Merchant City validation fails, the Add Transaction screen is refreshed and redisplayed to the user with the error message populated in the message area, the screen header updated with current date and time, and the cursor positioned on the Merchant City field so the user can correct the missing value.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Add Transaction screen and has successfully passed all prior mandatory field validations (Type Code, Category Code, Source, Description, Amount, Original Date, Processing Date, Merchant ID, Merchant Name, and Merchant City are all provided and valid)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user submits the Add Transaction screen and the Merchant Zip field is empty or contains only blank spaces
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) Set the error flag to 'Y' (error condition active), (2) Set the error message to 'Merchant Zip can NOT be empty...', (3) Highlight the Merchant Zip input field by setting its cursor position indicator, (4) Redisplay the Add Transaction screen with the error message visible, and (5) Halt further validation and transaction processing, awaiting user correction of the Merchant Zip field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Merchant Zip Mandatory Presence Check
all_rules.Rule_Description: Ensures that the Merchant Zip field is provided before a transaction can be added. If the Merchant Zip is left blank or empty, the system flags an error, displays a descriptive message, highlights the Merchant Zip field, and returns the Add Transaction screen to the user for correction. If Merchant Zip is present, validation proceeds to the Confirmation Check.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Add Transaction screen and has successfully passed all prior mandatory field validations (Type Code, Category Code, Source, Description, Amount, Original Date, Processing Date, Merchant ID, Merchant Name, and Merchant City are all provided and valid)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user submits the Add Transaction screen and the Merchant Zip field contains at least one non-blank, non-empty character
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) Allow the Merchant Zip validation to pass without setting any error flag or error message, (2) Not redisplay the screen due to a Merchant Zip error, and (3) Proceed to the Confirmation Check step where the user's confirmation response (Y/N) is evaluated

all_rules.Rule_Name: Merchant Zip Presence Check - Validation Pass
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Merchant Zip field contains a non-blank, non-empty value, the mandatory presence check passes and the transaction processing flow proceeds to the Confirmation Check stage.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All input validations for the transaction have passed successfully, and the Add Transaction screen is displayed to the user with the Confirmation field available for input
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user enters 'Y' (uppercase) or 'y' (lowercase) in the Confirmation field and submits the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system proceeds to execute the Add Transaction process to save the new transaction record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Proceed to Add Transaction on Positive Confirmation
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all input validations have passed, if the user explicitly confirms the transaction addition by entering 'Y' or 'y' in the Confirmation field, the system proceeds to add the transaction record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All input validations for the transaction have passed successfully, and the Add Transaction screen is displayed to the user with the Confirmation field available for input
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user enters 'N' (uppercase), 'n' (lowercase), or leaves the Confirmation field blank (spaces or not provided) and submits the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets an error condition, displays the message 'Confirm to add this transaction...' on the screen, positions the cursor on the Confirmation field, and re-displays the Add Transaction screen to the user without saving the transaction

all_rules.Rule_Name: Prompt for Confirmation When User Declines or Leaves Confirmation Blank
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all input validations have passed, if the user enters 'N', 'n', or leaves the Confirmation field blank (empty or not provided), the system does not add the transaction and instead re-displays the screen with a prompt message asking the user to confirm, with the cursor positioned on the Confirmation field.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All input validations for the transaction have passed successfully, and the Add Transaction screen is displayed to the user with the Confirmation field available for input
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user enters any value in the Confirmation field that is not 'Y', 'y', 'N', 'n', or blank (spaces/not provided) and submits the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets an error condition, displays the message 'Invalid value. Valid values are (Y/N)...' on the screen, positions the cursor on the Confirmation field, and re-displays the Add Transaction screen to the user without saving the transaction

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reject Invalid Confirmation Value
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all input validations have passed, if the user enters any value other than 'Y', 'y', 'N', 'n', or blank in the Confirmation field, the system treats it as an invalid entry, re-displays the screen with an error message, and positions the cursor on the Confirmation field.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is about to generate a new unique Transaction ID for a new transaction record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Transaction ID generation process is initiated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The search position is set to the highest possible value (HIGH-VALUES) so that the backward browse of the Transaction File will start from the logical end of the file and retrieve the last used Transaction ID

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Starting Position for Transaction ID Lookup
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before searching for the last used Transaction ID, the system must position the search pointer at the highest possible value so that the backward browse retrieves the most recently assigned Transaction ID.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The search position has been set to the highest possible value and the system needs to find the last used Transaction ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system attempts to open the Transaction File for backward browsing using the highest key position as the starting point
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction File browse is successfully opened, allowing the system to read backwards through transaction records to find the most recently assigned Transaction ID

all_rules.Rule_Name: Open Transaction File for Backward Browse
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system must open the Transaction File for backward browsing starting from the highest key position in order to locate the last used Transaction ID.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has attempted to open the Transaction File for backward browsing to find the last used Transaction ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Transaction File browse fails to open due to any unexpected error condition
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The error flag is set to indicate a failure, the message 'Unable to lookup Transaction...' is displayed to the user, the cursor is positioned on the Account ID field, and the Add Transaction screen is redisplayed — preventing the transaction from being added

all_rules.Rule_Name: Handle Transaction File Browse Open Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the Transaction File cannot be opened for backward browsing, the system must stop the transaction addition process and notify the user with an appropriate error message.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction File has been successfully opened for backward browsing from the highest key position
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system reads the previous record from the Transaction File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The last used Transaction ID is successfully retrieved from the most recent transaction record in the file, and this value is stored for use in generating the next Transaction ID

all_rules.Rule_Name: Read Last Transaction Record to Retrieve Highest Transaction ID
all_rules.Rule_Description: After successfully opening the Transaction File for backward browsing, the system reads the previous (last) record to retrieve the highest currently assigned Transaction ID, which will be used as the basis for generating the next unique Transaction ID.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction File has been successfully opened for backward browsing and the system attempts to read the last transaction record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The backward read reaches the end of file, indicating that no transaction records exist in the Transaction File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction ID is set to zero (0) as the baseline, so that when incremented by 1, the first transaction in the system will be assigned Transaction ID 1

all_rules.Rule_Name: Handle Empty Transaction File During ID Generation
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the Transaction File contains no records (end of file is reached immediately during backward browse), the system must treat the last used Transaction ID as zero, so that the first transaction will be assigned Transaction ID 1.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction File has been successfully opened for backward browsing and the system attempts to read the last transaction record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The read operation fails due to any unexpected error condition other than end-of-file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The error flag is set to indicate a failure, the message 'Unable to lookup Transaction...' is displayed to the user, the cursor is positioned on the Account ID field, and the Add Transaction screen is redisplayed — preventing the transaction from being added

all_rules.Rule_Name: Handle Transaction Record Read Failure During ID Generation
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the system encounters an unexpected error while reading the last transaction record during backward browse, the transaction addition process must be halted and the user must be notified.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The backward browse of the Transaction File has completed, either by successfully reading the last transaction record or by determining the file is empty
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system closes the Transaction File browse session
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction File browse is terminated and the system proceeds to calculate the new unique Transaction ID based on the retrieved last Transaction ID value

all_rules.Rule_Name: Close Transaction File Browse After ID Retrieval
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the last Transaction ID has been retrieved (or determined to be zero for an empty file), the Transaction File browse session must be closed before proceeding to generate the new Transaction ID.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The last used Transaction ID has been successfully retrieved from the Transaction File (or set to zero if the file was empty) and the Transaction File browse has been closed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system calculates the new Transaction ID
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The new Transaction ID is computed as the last used Transaction ID plus 1 (Last Transaction ID + 1), producing a sequentially unique identifier that will be assigned to the new transaction record being added

all_rules.Rule_Name: Generate New Unique Transaction ID by Incrementing Last Used ID
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system generates a new unique Transaction ID by taking the last used Transaction ID retrieved from the Transaction File and incrementing it by exactly 1. This ensures sequential, unique Transaction IDs are assigned to each new transaction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has passed all input validations for Account/Card Number and all transaction data fields, and has confirmed the intent to add a new transaction by entering 'Y' in the Confirm field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system begins the process of creating a new transaction record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must initialize the transaction record to a completely blank/empty state, clearing all fields, before any new data is written into it

all_rules.Rule_Name: Initialize a Blank Transaction Record Before Population
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before populating any fields, a new transaction record must be initialized to a clean/blank state to ensure no residual or stale data from previous operations contaminates the new transaction entry.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The transaction record has been initialized to a blank state and the system has retrieved the most recently added transaction's ID from the transaction file by browsing to the end of the file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system generates the new Transaction ID
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must take the last existing Transaction ID, add 1 to it to produce the next sequential Transaction ID, and assign this newly generated Transaction ID to the new transaction record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Auto-Generate and Assign a Unique Transaction ID to the New Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system automatically determines the next available Transaction ID by reading the last (highest) existing Transaction ID from the transaction file and incrementing it by 1. This generated ID is then assigned to the new transaction record. The user does not manually enter a Transaction ID.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A new transaction record has been initialized and assigned a Transaction ID, and the user has provided a valid numeric Transaction Type Code on the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the transaction record fields
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must copy the Transaction Type Code value entered by the user directly onto the transaction record's Type Code field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Assign Transaction Type Code from User Input to Transaction Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Transaction Type Code entered by the user on the Add Transaction screen is recorded onto the new transaction record. This field has already been validated as non-empty and numeric prior to this step.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The transaction record has been partially populated with Transaction ID and Type Code, and the user has provided a valid numeric Transaction Category Code on the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system continues populating the transaction record fields
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must copy the Transaction Category Code value entered by the user directly onto the transaction record's Category Code field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Assign Transaction Category Code from User Input to Transaction Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Transaction Category Code entered by the user on the Add Transaction screen is recorded onto the new transaction record. This field has already been validated as non-empty and numeric prior to this step.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The transaction record has been partially populated with Transaction ID, Type Code, and Category Code, and the user has provided a valid Transaction Source on the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system continues populating the transaction record fields
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must copy the Transaction Source value entered by the user directly onto the transaction record's Source field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Assign Transaction Source from User Input to Transaction Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Transaction Source entered by the user on the Add Transaction screen is recorded onto the new transaction record. This field has already been validated as non-empty prior to this step.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The transaction record has been partially populated with Transaction ID, Type Code, Category Code, and Source, and the user has provided a valid Transaction Description on the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system continues populating the transaction record fields
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must copy the Transaction Description value entered by the user directly onto the transaction record's Description field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Assign Transaction Description from User Input to Transaction Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Transaction Description entered by the user on the Add Transaction screen is recorded onto the new transaction record. This field has already been validated as non-empty prior to this step.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The transaction record has been partially populated and the user has provided a valid Transaction Amount in the format ±99999999.99 (e.g., -00012345.67 or +00012345.67) which has already passed format and content validation
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system processes the Transaction Amount for storage
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must convert the character-formatted amount string into a numeric value using a numeric conversion function (NUMVAL-C), and then assign the resulting numeric amount to the transaction record's Amount field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Convert Transaction Amount to Numeric Value and Assign to Transaction Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Transaction Amount entered by the user in the format ±99999999.99 must be converted from its display/character representation into a true numeric value before being stored on the transaction record. This ensures the amount is stored in a computationally usable numeric format.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The transaction record has been partially populated and a valid Card Number is present on the screen — either entered directly by the user or auto-populated from the Account ID cross-reference lookup
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system continues populating the transaction record fields
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must copy the Card Number value from the screen onto the transaction record's Card Number field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Assign Card Number from User Input to Transaction Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Card Number associated with the transaction is recorded onto the new transaction record. This is the card number that was either entered directly by the user or auto-populated via Account ID cross-reference lookup, and has already been validated.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The transaction record has been partially populated with Transaction ID, Type Code, Category Code, Source, Description, Amount, and Card Number, and the user has provided a valid numeric Merchant ID on the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system continues populating the transaction record fields
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must copy the Merchant ID value entered by the user directly onto the transaction record's Merchant ID field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Assign Merchant ID from User Input to Transaction Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Merchant ID entered by the user on the Add Transaction screen is recorded onto the new transaction record. This field has already been validated as non-empty and numeric prior to this step.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The transaction record has been partially populated including Merchant ID, and the user has provided a valid Merchant Name on the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system continues populating the transaction record fields
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must copy the Merchant Name value entered by the user directly onto the transaction record's Merchant Name field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Assign Merchant Name from User Input to Transaction Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Merchant Name entered by the user on the Add Transaction screen is recorded onto the new transaction record. This field has already been validated as non-empty prior to this step.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The transaction record has been partially populated including Merchant ID and Merchant Name, and the user has provided a valid Merchant City on the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system continues populating the transaction record fields
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must copy the Merchant City value entered by the user directly onto the transaction record's Merchant City field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Assign Merchant City from User Input to Transaction Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Merchant City entered by the user on the Add Transaction screen is recorded onto the new transaction record. This field has already been validated as non-empty prior to this step.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The transaction record has been partially populated including Merchant ID, Merchant Name, and Merchant City, and the user has provided a valid Merchant Zip Code on the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system continues populating the transaction record fields
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must copy the Merchant Zip Code value entered by the user directly onto the transaction record's Merchant Zip field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Assign Merchant Zip Code from User Input to Transaction Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Merchant Zip Code entered by the user on the Add Transaction screen is recorded onto the new transaction record. This field has already been validated as non-empty prior to this step.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The transaction record has been partially populated with all merchant details, and the user has provided a valid Origination Date in YYYY-MM-DD format that has passed both format and calendar validity checks
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system continues populating the transaction record fields
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must copy the Origination Date value entered by the user directly onto the transaction record's Origination Date/Timestamp field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Assign Transaction Origination Date from User Input to Transaction Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Transaction Origination Date entered by the user on the Add Transaction screen is recorded onto the new transaction record. This field has already been validated as non-empty, correctly formatted as YYYY-MM-DD, and confirmed as a real calendar date prior to this step.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The transaction record has been populated with all required fields including Origination Date, and the user has provided a valid Processing Date in YYYY-MM-DD format that has passed both format and calendar validity checks
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sets the final field on the transaction record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must copy the Processing Date value entered by the user directly onto the transaction record's Processing Date/Timestamp field, completing the population of all transaction record fields and making the record ready to be written to the transaction file

all_rules.Rule_Name: Assign Transaction Processing Date from User Input to Transaction Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Transaction Processing Date entered by the user on the Add Transaction screen is recorded onto the new transaction record. This field has already been validated as non-empty, correctly formatted as YYYY-MM-DD, and confirmed as a real calendar date prior to this step. This is the final field populated before the record is written to the transaction file.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A new transaction record has been fully populated with: auto-generated Transaction ID, Transaction Type Code, Category Code, Source, Description, Amount, Card Number, Merchant ID, Merchant Name, Merchant City, Merchant Zip, Original Date, and Processing Date
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system attempts to write the new transaction record to the Transaction File using the auto-generated Transaction ID as the record key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction File receives the new record and returns a write outcome (Successful Write, Duplicate Transaction ID, or Write Failure)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Write New Transaction Record to Transaction File
all_rules.Rule_Description: When all validations pass and the user confirms, the system attempts to persist the new transaction record with all its details into the Transaction File.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has successfully written the new transaction record to the Transaction File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The write operation returns a successful outcome
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All input fields on the Add Transaction screen are cleared to spaces, including: Account ID, Card Number, Transaction Type Code, Category Code, Source, Amount, Description, Original Date, Processing Date, Merchant ID, Merchant Name, Merchant City, Merchant Zip, and Confirm field; and the cursor is repositioned to the Account ID field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Successful Transaction Write - Clear Form and Build Success Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: Upon a successful write of the new transaction record, the system clears all input fields on the Add Transaction screen, resetting the form to a blank state ready for a new entry.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The new transaction record has been successfully written to the Transaction File and all input fields have been cleared
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system builds the success confirmation message
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system constructs the message by concatenating: the text 'Transaction added successfully. ', followed by ' Your Tran ID is ', followed by the newly assigned Transaction ID value (trimmed of trailing spaces), followed by a period '.'; the complete message is stored in the screen message field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Successful Transaction Write - Construct Success Message with Transaction ID
all_rules.Rule_Description: After a successful transaction write and form reset, the system constructs a confirmation message that includes the newly assigned Transaction ID so the user can reference the transaction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The success message containing the new Transaction ID has been constructed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Add Transaction screen is refreshed and displayed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The success message is displayed in green color in the message area of the Add Transaction screen, confirming the transaction was added and showing the assigned Transaction ID

all_rules.Rule_Name: Successful Transaction Write - Display Success Message in Green
all_rules.Rule_Description: The success confirmation message is displayed to the user in green color on the Add Transaction screen to visually distinguish it from error messages.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has attempted to write a new transaction record to the Transaction File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The write operation returns a Duplicate Transaction ID outcome (either duplicate key or duplicate record condition)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The error flag is set to indicate an error condition; the error message 'Tran ID already exist...' is displayed in the message area of the Add Transaction screen; the cursor is positioned on the Account ID field; the Add Transaction screen is refreshed and redisplayed with the error

all_rules.Rule_Name: Duplicate Transaction ID - Reject Write and Display Error
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the auto-generated Transaction ID already exists in the Transaction File (duplicate key condition), the system rejects the write and informs the user that the Transaction ID is already in use.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has attempted to write a new transaction record to the Transaction File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The write operation returns a failure outcome that is neither a successful write nor a duplicate Transaction ID condition
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The error flag is set to indicate an error condition; the error message 'Unable to Add Transaction...' is displayed in the message area of the Add Transaction screen; the cursor is positioned on the Account ID field; the Add Transaction screen is refreshed and redisplayed with the error

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transaction Write Failure - Display System Error
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the transaction write fails for any reason other than a duplicate Transaction ID, the system informs the user that the transaction could not be added.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The write operation to the Transaction File has completed with any outcome (success, duplicate Transaction ID, or write failure)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to return control to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system populates the screen header with current date and time, program name, and transaction name; displays the appropriate message (success in green or error) in the message area; and sends the refreshed Add Transaction screen (map COTRN2A from mapset COTRN02) to the user's terminal, returning control with the current transaction ID and communication area preserved

all_rules.Rule_Name: Refresh and Display Add Transaction Screen After Write Outcome
all_rules.Rule_Description: Regardless of the write outcome (success, duplicate, or failure), the Add Transaction screen is always refreshed and redisplayed to the user with the appropriate message.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A transaction has been successfully added and saved to the transaction file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system performs the post-success field initialization

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear Account ID and Card Number After Successful Transaction Add
all_rules.Rule_Description: After a transaction is successfully written to the system, the Account ID and Card Number input fields must be cleared to blank so the form is ready for a new transaction entry.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A transaction has been successfully added and saved to the transaction file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system performs the post-success field initialization
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction Type Code field (TTYPCDI), Category Code field (TCATCDI), Source field (TRNSRCI), Amount field (TRNAMTI), and Description field (TDESCI) on the Add Transaction screen are all cleared to spaces

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear Transaction Detail Fields After Successful Transaction Add
all_rules.Rule_Description: After a transaction is successfully saved, all transaction detail fields — Transaction Type Code, Category Code, Source, Amount, and Description — must be cleared to blank to prepare the screen for a new transaction entry.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A transaction has been successfully added and saved to the transaction file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system performs the post-success field initialization
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Origination Date field (TORIGDTI) and Processing Date field (TPROCDTI) on the Add Transaction screen are both cleared to spaces

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear Date Fields After Successful Transaction Add
all_rules.Rule_Description: After a transaction is successfully saved, the Origination Date and Processing Date fields must be cleared to blank so the form is ready for a new transaction entry.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A transaction has been successfully added and saved to the transaction file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system performs the post-success field initialization
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Merchant ID field (MIDI), Merchant Name field (MNAMEI), Merchant City field (MCITYI), and Merchant Zip field (MZIPI) on the Add Transaction screen are all cleared to spaces

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear Merchant Fields After Successful Transaction Add
all_rules.Rule_Description: After a transaction is successfully saved, all merchant-related fields — Merchant ID, Merchant Name, Merchant City, and Merchant Zip — must be cleared to blank to prepare the screen for a new transaction entry.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A transaction has been successfully added and saved to the transaction file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system performs the post-success field initialization
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Confirmation field (CONFIRMI) and the working storage message area (WS-MESSAGE) are both cleared to spaces

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear Confirmation Field and Message Area After Successful Transaction Add
all_rules.Rule_Description: After a transaction is successfully saved, the Confirmation field and the message area must be cleared to blank so the screen is clean and ready for a new transaction entry before the success message is composed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A transaction has been successfully added and saved, and all input fields have been cleared
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system composes the post-success confirmation message
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The message area (WS-MESSAGE) is populated with the text 'Transaction added successfully. Your Tran ID is [TRAN-ID].' where [TRAN-ID] is the auto-generated Transaction ID assigned to the newly created transaction, and the message color attribute (ERRMSGC) is set to green to visually indicate success

all_rules.Rule_Name: Compose Success Message with Newly Assigned Transaction ID
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all fields are cleared following a successful transaction save, the system must compose and display a success message that includes the newly assigned Transaction ID, so the user has a reference for the transaction just created. The message is displayed in green color to indicate success.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All input fields have been cleared and the success message with the new Transaction ID has been composed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sends the refreshed Add Transaction screen to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Add Transaction screen (COTRN2A in mapset COTRN02) is displayed with: all input fields blank, the success message 'Transaction added successfully. Your Tran ID is [TRAN-ID].' shown in green in the message area, the screen header populated with current date and time, program name, and transaction name, and the cursor positioned at the Account ID field ready for new input

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Refreshed Add Transaction Screen Ready for New Entry
all_rules.Rule_Description: After composing the success message, the system must redisplay the Add Transaction screen in a fully cleared state with the success message visible, the current date and time in the header, and the cursor positioned at the Account ID field, so the user can immediately begin entering a new transaction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Add Transaction screen is about to be displayed to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen header population process is initiated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system retrieves the current system date and time and stores it in the working date/time data area (WS-CURDATE-DATA), making the current month, day, year, hours, minutes, and seconds available for subsequent header field population

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retrieve Current System Date and Time for Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before populating the screen header, the system retrieves the current system date and time so that accurate date and time values can be displayed to the user on the Add Transaction screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen header population process is in progress and the current system date and time have been retrieved
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the first title line of the screen header
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The application's first title line (CCDA-TITLE01) is copied into the Title Line 1 output field (TITLE01O) of the Add Transaction screen header

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Application Title Line 1 on Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: The first line of the application title, sourced from the application's central title definition (CCDA-TITLE01), is placed into the screen header area so that users can identify the application they are working within.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen header population process is in progress and Title Line 1 has been populated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the second title line of the screen header
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The application's second title line (CCDA-TITLE02) is copied into the Title Line 2 output field (TITLE02O) of the Add Transaction screen header

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Application Title Line 2 on Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: The second line of the application title, sourced from the application's central title definition (CCDA-TITLE02), is placed into the screen header area to complete the application identification displayed to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen header population process is in progress and both application title lines have been populated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the transaction identifier field of the screen header
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current transaction ID (WS-TRANID) is copied into the Transaction Name output field (TRNNAMEO) of the Add Transaction screen header

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Transaction ID on Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: The current transaction identifier (the CICS transaction ID under which the program is running) is displayed in the screen header so that users and support staff can identify the active transaction context.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen header population process is in progress and the transaction ID has been populated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the program name field of the screen header
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current program name (WS-PGMNAME) is copied into the Program Name output field (PGMNAMEO) of the Add Transaction screen header

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Program Name on Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: The name of the currently executing program is displayed in the screen header so that users and support staff can identify which program is being executed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen header population process is in progress, the program name has been populated, and the current system date has been retrieved into WS-CURDATE-DATA containing separate month (WS-CURDATE-MONTH), day (WS-CURDATE-DAY), and 4-digit year (WS-CURDATE-YEAR) components
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system formats the current date for display in the screen header
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current month is moved to WS-CURDATE-MM, the current day is moved to WS-CURDATE-DD, and only the last two digits of the current year (positions 3-4 of WS-CURDATE-YEAR) are moved to WS-CURDATE-YY; the resulting MM-DD-YY formatted date (WS-CURDATE-MM-DD-YY) is then placed into the Current Date output field (CURDATEO) of the Add Transaction screen header

all_rules.Rule_Name: Format and Display Current Date as MM-DD-YY on Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: The current system date is formatted into the MM-DD-YY display format for presentation in the screen header. The year is represented as a 2-digit value extracted from the last two digits of the 4-digit year.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen header population process is in progress, the formatted date has been populated, and the current system time has been retrieved into WS-CURDATE-DATA containing separate hours (WS-CURTIME-HOURS), minutes (WS-CURTIME-MINUTE), and seconds (WS-CURTIME-SECOND) components
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system formats the current time for display in the screen header
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current hours are moved to WS-CURTIME-HH, the current minutes are moved to WS-CURTIME-MM, and the current seconds are moved to WS-CURTIME-SS; the resulting HH-MM-SS formatted time (WS-CURTIME-HH-MM-SS) is then placed into the Current Time output field (CURTIMEO) of the Add Transaction screen header

all_rules.Rule_Name: Format and Display Current Time as HH-MM-SS on Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: The current system time is formatted into the HH-MM-SS display format for presentation in the screen header, using hours, minutes, and seconds components extracted from the retrieved system time.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Add Transaction screen is being prepared for display to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system initiates the screen population process
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system retrieves the current system date and time using the CURRENT-DATE function and stores it in the working storage date-time field (WS-CURDATE-DATA), making both date components (year, month, day) and time components (hours, minutes, seconds) available for subsequent header population

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retrieve Current System Date and Time for Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: When preparing the Add Transaction screen for display, the system must retrieve the current system date and time to populate the screen header with accurate timestamp information.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Add Transaction screen header is being populated and the application title constants (CCDA-TITLE01 and CCDA-TITLE02) are defined in the common application data area
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the screen header fields
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system copies Application Title Line 1 (CCDA-TITLE01) into the screen output field TITLE01O and Application Title Line 2 (CCDA-TITLE02) into the screen output field TITLE02O of the Add Transaction screen map (COTRN2AO)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Application Title Lines in Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Add Transaction screen header must display the standard application title on two lines, sourced from the centrally defined application constants, to provide consistent branding and context to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Add Transaction screen header is being populated and the current Transaction ID (WS-TRANID) and Program Name (WS-PGMNAME) are available in working storage
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the screen header fields
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system copies the Transaction ID (WS-TRANID) into the screen output field TRNNAMEO and the Program Name (WS-PGMNAME) into the screen output field PGMNAMEO of the Add Transaction screen map (COTRN2AO)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Transaction ID and Program Name in Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Add Transaction screen header must display the current transaction identifier and the program name to allow users and support staff to identify the active transaction and program context.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current system date has been retrieved and stored in WS-CURDATE-DATA, with individual components available as WS-CURDATE-MONTH (month), WS-CURDATE-DAY (day), and WS-CURDATE-YEAR (4-digit year)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system formats the current date for the screen header
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system extracts the 2-digit month into WS-CURDATE-MM, the 2-digit day into WS-CURDATE-DD, and the last 2 digits of the year (positions 3-4 of WS-CURDATE-YEAR) into WS-CURDATE-YY, then assembles these into the MM-DD-YY formatted field WS-CURDATE-MM-DD-YY and copies it into the screen output field CURDATEO of the Add Transaction screen map (COTRN2AO)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Format and Display Current Date in MM-DD-YY Format on Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Add Transaction screen header must display the current date formatted as MM-DD-YY (2-digit month, 2-digit day, 2-digit year) to provide the user with a recognizable and standardized date reference.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current system time has been retrieved and stored in WS-CURDATE-DATA, with individual components available as WS-CURTIME-HOURS (hours), WS-CURTIME-MINUTE (minutes), and WS-CURTIME-SECOND (seconds)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system formats the current time for the screen header
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system extracts the 2-digit hours into WS-CURTIME-HH, the 2-digit minutes into WS-CURTIME-MM, and the 2-digit seconds into WS-CURTIME-SS, then assembles these into the HH-MM-SS formatted field WS-CURTIME-HH-MM-SS and copies it into the screen output field CURTIMEO of the Add Transaction screen map (COTRN2AO)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Format and Display Current Time in HH-MM-SS Format on Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Add Transaction screen header must display the current time formatted as HH-MM-SS (2-digit hours, 2-digit minutes, 2-digit seconds) to provide the user with an accurate time reference on the screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A validation error message or status message has been set in the working storage message field (WS-MESSAGE) — this may be a field-level validation error (e.g., 'Account ID must be Numeric...', 'Amount can NOT be empty...', 'Orig Date should be in format YYYY-MM-DD'), a lookup error (e.g., 'Account ID NOT found...', 'Card Number NOT found...'), a confirmation prompt (e.g., 'Confirm to add this transaction...'), a success message (e.g., 'Transaction added successfully. Your Tran ID is [ID].'), or an invalid key message
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the Add Transaction screen for display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system copies the contents of WS-MESSAGE into the screen error/message output field ERRMSGO of the Add Transaction screen map (COTRN2AO), making the message visible to the user on the screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Validation or Status Message on Add Transaction Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: Any validation error message or status message generated during input processing must be transferred to the screen message field so the user receives clear feedback about the outcome of their action or the nature of any input error.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Add Transaction screen map (COTRN2AO) has been fully populated with header information, field data, and any validation or status messages
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sends the screen to the user terminal
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system transmits the Add Transaction screen using map name 'COTRN2A' from mapset 'COTRN02', erasing the previous terminal content (ERASE), and positioning the cursor at the field designated by the cursor control setting (CURSOR), so the user sees a fully refreshed screen with the cursor in the appropriate input position

all_rules.Rule_Name: Send Add Transaction Screen to User Terminal
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all header and message fields have been populated, the fully assembled Add Transaction screen must be transmitted to the user's terminal, erasing any previous screen content and positioning the cursor at the designated input field.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Add Transaction screen has been successfully sent to the user terminal
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system completes the current processing cycle
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system returns control to the CICS transaction manager, specifying the current Transaction ID (WS-TRANID) as the next transaction to be invoked when the user responds, and passing the current Communication Area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) to preserve the session context — including program state, navigation history, and any pre-selected transaction data — so that when the user presses a key, the same transaction resumes with full context intact

all_rules.Rule_Name: Await Next User Interaction by Returning Control with Transaction Context
all_rules.Rule_Description: After sending the screen, the system must suspend processing and wait for the user's next input. The current transaction identifier and the full communication area (containing session state) must be preserved and passed forward so the application can resume correctly when the user responds.

description:
COTRN02C is a CICS online program within the CardDemo application that enables users to add a new transaction record to the TRANSACT file. The program validates user-entered transaction details (including account/card number lookup, transaction type, category, amount, dates, and merchant information) and writes a new transaction record with an auto-generated sequential transaction ID. It is a main/driver program that controls screen interaction, data validation, and file operations independently.
- **Execution Environment**: Online (CICS) - **Database Access**: VSAM/CICS Files - **MQ Calls**: No - **Module Type**: Main/Driver module
### Key Functionalities: 1: Program Initialization - Initialize error flags, user-modified flags, and clear message fields at the start of each program invocation 2: Session Validation - Check if communication area length is zero; if so, redirect unauthenticated users to the sign-on screen 3: First-Time Screen Display - On first entry to the program, initialize the transaction add screen and pre-populate card number if a transaction was selected from a prior screen, then display the Add Transaction screen 4: Screen Input Reception - Receive user input from the Add Transaction screen on subsequent visits 5: Enter Key Processing - Route to input validation and transaction add logic when user presses Enter 6: Navigate Back - When user presses PF3, return to the calling program (or default menu) passing control back via the communication area 7: Clear Screen - When user presses PF4, clear all input fields on the Add Transaction screen and redisplay a blank form 8: Copy Last Transaction Data - When user presses PF5, retrieve the most recently added transaction for the given account/card and pre-populate all transaction detail fields on the screen for the user to review or modify 9: Invalid Key Handling - For any unrecognized function key, display an invalid key message to the user 10: Account ID Validation - If the user enters an Account ID, verify it is numeric; if not, display an error message 11: Account ID Lookup - Look up the entered Account ID in the cross-reference index file to retrieve the associated Card Number; if not found, display an error message 12: Card Number Validation - If the user enters a Card Number instead of Account ID, verify it is numeric; if not, display an error message 13: Card Number Lookup - Look up the entered Card Number in the cross-reference file to retrieve the associated Account ID; if not found, display an error message 14: Account or Card Number Presence Check - Ensure that at least one of Account ID or Card Number is provided; if both are missing, display an error message 15: Transaction Type Code Validation - Verify that Transaction Type Code is not empty and is numeric; display appropriate error messages if invalid 16: Transaction Category Code Validation - Verify that Transaction Category Code is not empty and is numeric; display appropriate error messages if invalid 17: Transaction Source Validation - Verify that Transaction Source field is not empty; display an error message if missing 18: Transaction Description Validation - Verify that Transaction Description is not empty; display an error message if missing 19: Transaction Amount Validation - Verify that Transaction Amount is not empty and conforms to the required format (sign followed by 8 digits, decimal point, 2 decimal digits); display an error message if invalid 20: Origination Date Format Validation - Verify that the Origination Date is not empty and conforms to YYYY-MM-DD format; display an error message if invalid 21: Processing Date Format Validation - Verify that the Processing Date is not empty and conforms to YYYY-MM-DD format; display an error message if invalid 22: Origination Date Calendar Validation - Call the date validation utility to confirm the Origination Date is a real calendar date; display an error message if the date is invalid 23: Processing Date Calendar Validation - Call the date validation utility to confirm the Processing Date is a real calendar date; display an error message if the date is invalid 24: Merchant ID Validation - Verify that Merchant ID is not empty and is numeric; display an error message if invalid 25: Merchant Name Validation - Verify that Merchant Name is not empty; display an error message if missing 26: Merchant City Validation - Verify that Merchant City is not empty; display an error message if missing 27: Merchant Zip Validation - Verify that Merchant Zip is not empty; display an error message if missing 28: Confirmation Check - After all validations pass, check if the user has confirmed the transaction add (Y/N); prompt for confirmation if not provided, or show error for invalid confirmation value 29: New Transaction ID Generation - Browse the transaction file from the highest key backwards to find the last used Transaction ID, then increment it by 1 to generate a new unique Transaction ID 30: Transaction Record Creation - Populate a new transaction record with all validated input fields including type code, category code, source, description, amount, card number, merchant details, origination date, and processing date 31: Transaction Record Write - Write the new transaction record to the transaction file; display a success message with the new Transaction ID upon successful write, or display an error message if a duplicate or write failure occurs 32: Screen Clear After Success - After a successful transaction add, clear all input fields and reset the form for a new entry 33: Screen Header Population - Populate the screen header with application title, program name, transaction ID, current date, and current time before displaying the screen 34: Add Transaction Screen Display - Send the populated Add Transaction screen to the user terminal, displaying any validation or status messages
